eligibility.quote: according to the following gdb debug, it seems that created subscription is not added to `rmw_wait` to be executed for Fast-DDS case. So subscription will never be executed by executer.
eligibility.reason: The report reproduces lost notification across rclcpp's use of rmw_fastrtps's wait/guard-condition API. These separately released libraries form a PAIR; the fact that two executor threads contend does not make them two separately deployed CONCURRENT units. E1-E4 hold.

failed_conditions.quote:
*   - It is not safe to wait for the same entity using different wait sets in two or
 *     more threads concurrently.
failed_conditions.reason: This is an explicit exclusive-use restriction on a shared wait entity. The node notify guard condition and its wait/trigger operations are implicated. It is not a ROS hardware resource-claim error, but the exclusive-resource class fits the documented prohibition.

loudness.reason: The observed symptom is a subscription that never executes; the report shows no build, connection, or activation diagnostic rejecting this API usage. A manually obtained debugger trace is not such a diagnostic.

detection_stage.quote: So subscription will never be executed by executer.
detection_stage.reason: The missing callbacks are observed during execution, hence run.

resolution.quote: We are currently working on a solution for this (#619) which fixes this issue for us locally. It is still missing some work which will be ready this week.
resolution.reason: The proposed provider change has local success evidence, but that statement does not identify both tested unit revisions. It does not establish observed for the specification's resolved pair.

supporting_evidence.quote: The main motivation is to fix bugs related to the current "waitset" mechanism implemented on top of Fast-DDS listeners, like #613.

notes: The resource token is an analyst-assigned name for the actual node guard condition, not a literal ROS resource name. Changing to CycloneDDS demonstrates provider dependence but is a different provider composition.
